# Shopify app icon: specification, artifacts, and where to pick the design back up

Research and design record for Baton's app icon. Covers Shopify's requirements, the artifacts
the icon produces and where they live, the toolchain that builds and verifies them, and the
design history — what was drawn, what was rejected, and why — so a later session can resume
iterating on the look without re-deriving any of it.

**Status: shipped 2026-09-21** — the `wisp` mark, generated by `pnpm icon` from
`scripts/icon.ts`. Measured 771 × 864 px of the 1200 px canvas, margins 214/215/167/169
(l/r/t/b), inside every Shopify constraint. The look is explicitly **not** considered final;
§6 is the pick-up point.

---

## 1. The current mark

One baton, thrown, and three whooshes for the air behind it, on cobalt.

| Role             | Value            |
| ---------------- | ---------------- |
| Ground           | Cobalt `#1F4FD8` |
| Baton            | Amber `#FFC24B`  |
| Whoosh, nearest  | White `#FFFFFF`  |
| Whoosh, middle   | `#AFC4F7`        |
| Whoosh, furthest | `#6E90EC`        |

Three rules hold the drawing together. They are stated normatively in `scripts/icon.ts` and in
the comment at the top of `public/app-icon.svg`; they are repeated here only because a design
session starts in this document.

1. **Nothing touches the baton.** Anything it rests against anchors it, and an anchored baton
   reads as a part in a machine rather than an object in motion.
2. **The motion is never another baton.** A ghosted, repeated or trailing copy reads as two
   objects, not as one object moving. The air is drawn with shapes that are not batons.
3. **The baton is steeper than its own travel.** A thrown baton tumbles, so it is not aligned
   with the direction it is going. That mismatch (baton at −72°, whooshes running shallow) is
   the only thing stopping the whooshes from reading as more batons. Aligning them collapses
   the mark into a row of parallel bars.

The whooshes are **calligraphic**: closed outlines that swell to a belly and close to a point at
both ends. A round-capped stroke shares the baton's own vocabulary and reads as a second,
stunted baton. Their bellies sit at different fractions of their length (0.60 / 0.54 / 0.46),
with different lengths and arcs, because three matched strokes read as a rigid grille.

The three whoosh tints step from white toward the ground colour. That is dissipation done in
**block colour on purpose** — see §4 for the gradient test that rejected the obvious approach.

## 2. Shopify's specification

Sources, both in `refs/shopify-docs`, cited by file and heading (never line number, which does
not survive a `pnpm refs fetch`):

- `docs/apps/design/visual-design.md`, "App icon" → specifications, the icon grid, the
  background warning.
- `docs/apps/launch/shopify-app-store/best-practices.md`, "2. App icon" → the content rules.
- `docs/apps/launch/shopify-app-store/app-store-requirements.md`, §4.1–4.2 → naming and the
  ban on pricing in the logo.

| Property                                      | Requirement                                               | Baton                   |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Format                                        | PNG or JPG                                                | PNG                     |
| Canvas                                        | Exactly 1200 × 1200 px                                    | 1200 × 1200             |
| Corners                                       | Square — Shopify rounds them itself                       | Square                  |
| Artwork size                                  | Fill 10/16ths (750 px) to 12/16ths (900 px) of the canvas | 864 px on its long side |
| Clear margin                                  | At least 1/16th (75 px) free of any visual element        | 167 px at the tightest  |
| Background                                    | Legible on `#FFFFFF` **and** `#F1F1F1`                    | Solid cobalt            |
| Text                                          | Avoid                                                     | None                    |
| Screenshots, Shopify trademarks, other brands | Prohibited                                                | None                    |
| Pricing                                       | Never in the icon or logo                                 | None                    |

Two facts that shaped the design more than the table does:

- **Shopify re-renders the icon as an SVG in the admin's left navigation**, where it lands at
  roughly 20 px (`visual-design.md`, "App icon"). That size, not the App Store listing, is what
  a candidate mark has to survive. Every variant in §5 was rendered at 16/20/32/48 px against
  both admin backgrounds before it was judged.
- **The icon is uploaded in the Dev Dashboard**, on the app's Settings page. It is _not_ set
  from `shopify.app.toml`, so shipping the PNG to the repo does not ship it to Shopify.

### Distinctness from Shopify Flow

Flow's icon is a lime green tile carrying circular nodes joined by connecting lines, and it sits
in the same admin sidebar as Baton. Baton shares none of it: no green, no circular nodes, no
connectors, no node-graph. This is worth re-checking against any future direction, because a
"stations joined by a path" idea drifts straight into it — see the rejected `Handoff` family in
§5.

## 3. The artifacts

All four are written by `pnpm icon` (`scripts/icon.ts`). **None of them is hand-editable**: the
whoosh outlines are sampled curves, and hand-patching one of the four is how the app ends up
showing two different marks in the same browser tab.

| Artifact                       | What it is                                                                  |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `public/app-icon.svg`          | Source of truth. Square corners. Carries the mark's rationale in a comment. |
| `public/app-icon.png`          | The 1200 × 1200 upload for the Dev Dashboard. Rasterised from the SVG.      |
| `public/favicon.svg`           | Same mark, rounded corners. Served from `src/routes/__root.tsx`.            |
| `src/components/BatonMark.tsx` | The same drawing as a component, for every copy rendered inside the app.    |

Where the mark appears in the app:

| Surface             | File                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Browser tab         | `src/routes/__root.tsx` (`rel="icon"` → `/favicon.svg`)                                  |
| Public landing page | `src/routes/index.tsx` — 56 px, above the overview paragraph                             |
| Member login        | `src/routes/login.tsx` — 32 px, with the "Baton" wordmark, since the heading is "Log in" |
| Member area chrome  | `src/components/MemberBar.tsx` — 24 px, the link back to the queue                       |

The embedded app home (`src/routes/app.index.tsx`) deliberately carries **no** mark. It was tried
— 28 px with the tagline beside it — and cut on sight: Shopify already renders the icon in the
admin sidebar immediately beside that page, so the mark appeared twice on one screen, and with
`s-page` offering no slot above its heading the lockup floated in the page gutter above the first
card with nothing anchoring it. Do not re-add it without solving that anchoring problem.

### Still missing for an App Store submission

- The icon has to be **uploaded in the Dev Dashboard**; the repo copy does nothing by itself.
- Listing media (feature image, screenshots) does not exist yet. For reference, a sibling app
  keeps a 1600×900 hero and feature media alongside its icon.

## 4. Toolchain

```bash
pnpm icon   # writes all four artifacts, then re-measures against Shopify's grid
```

The script prints its own compliance check on every run, because the `scale`/`dx`/`dy` that seat
a drawing on the icon grid are only correct until someone edits the geometry:

```
  fit: mark 771 x 864, margins 214/215/167/169 (l/r/t/b)
  ok: long side 864px (Shopify wants 750-900)
  ok: tightest margin 167px (Shopify wants >= 75)
```

Three toolchain facts that cost time to discover:

1. **ImageMagick cannot rasterise these SVGs.** The `magick` build here has no `rsvg-convert`
   delegate and falls back to its own renderer, which silently drops `transform` attributes and
   emits a bare background tile — no error, no warning, just a blank blue square. Use headless
   Chrome's `--screenshot`, which `scripts/icon.ts` does.
2. **ImageMagick is still the right tool for measuring.** Adding a 1 px border in the ground
   colour and trimming with a small fuzz gives the mark's bounding box inside a full-bleed tile:
   `magick icon.png -bordercolor '#1F4FD8' -border 1 -fuzz 1% -trim info:-`.
3. **The generator must format its own output.** `pnpm fmt` and the generator disagreed about
   the emitted JSX, so every `pnpm icon` left a diff that the next `pnpm fmt` rewrote and the
   next `pnpm icon` rewrote back. `scripts/icon.ts` runs `oxfmt` over `BatonMark.tsx` itself.

### Changing the mark

Edit `VARIANTS` in `scripts/icon.ts` and re-run. A variant is a list of whooshes plus the
`scale`/`dx`/`dy` that centre the result.

| Parameter           | Effect                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `p0..p3`            | Cubic centreline of one whoosh.                                                                                                                      |
| `width`             | Belly width in canvas px.                                                                                                                            |
| `belly`             | Where along the stroke the belly sits, 0–1. Off-centre reads as brush-drawn; 0.5 reads as a leaf.                                                    |
| `ease`              | How fast the stroke closes toward its tips. Lower keeps body for longer; high values give claws.                                                     |
| `fill`              | One of the three air tints.                                                                                                                          |
| `scale`, `dx`, `dy` | Seat the drawing on Shopify's grid. Derive by rendering, reading the printed `fit:` line, and solving for a centred box with a long side of 750–900. |

`BATON_CENTRE`, `BATON_ANGLE`, `BATON_LENGTH` and `BATON_WIDTH` control the baton. `CURRENT`
selects which variant ships. Four variants are kept in the file (`dissipating`, `slipstream`,
`drift`, `wisp`) so alternatives can be compared by changing one constant.

## 5. Design history: what was rejected and why

Five rounds of review. Recorded so a later session does not re-walk them. The short version:
**every attempt to make the icon narrate the handoff made it more static**, and the mark only
came alive once it stopped explaining and just showed one object in flight.

### Round 1 — the metaphor, six directions

Concepts: `Pass` (two capsules mid-exchange), `Grip`, `Steps`, `Loop`, `Check`, `Relay`.

Rejected: all but `Pass`. **Verdict on `Pass`: "doesn't seem to indicate passing anything."** A
single tilted capsule split in two reads as a diagonal stroke, nothing more.

Also found here: the first `Pass` draft had its two capsules collinear and overlapping by 139 px,
so it rendered as one two-tone baton rather than two shapes. Caught by rendering, not by
arithmetic — a recurring lesson.

### Round 2 — stations

`Handoff`: two bars as the station finishing the work and the station taking it up, with the
baton lying across both. Also `In transit` and `In flight`.

Rejected. **Verdict: better, but "no bang… it's just kind of [sitting there]."** Diagnosis: the
baton was sized to fit politely between its two stations, and an object scaled to its container
reads as at rest. Also caught here: the baton sat 5 px from the lower rail and 47 px from the
upper one — unintentional, not an optical adjustment.

Note this family also drifts toward Shopify Flow's node-and-connector icon. Worth remembering if
"stations" is ever revisited.

### Round 3 — overshoot

`Through`: the same rails, but the baton steepened to 63° and overshooting both, so it drives
through rather than parking between.

Rejected, and the strongest signal of the whole process. **Verdict: "it looks worse… I don't like
the baton touching anything, it makes it look somehow too mechanical."** Diagnosis, which holds
for anything drawn later: **furniture is static by definition, and anything the baton touches
anchors it.** Narrating a handoff needs two fixed endpoints; motion needs none. The two goals
fight, and the narrative wins by default because it is easier to draw.

### Round 4 — nothing touching

`Arc` (baton plus a detached trajectory), `Strobe` (the same baton at two moments, rotating),
`Tumble` (three moments), `Ghost` (the earlier moment in a deeper blue).

Rejected. **Verdict: ghosts and repeated batons don't work — "maybe just the baton itself and
then some visual that indicates it's in motion."** Diagnosis: a repeated baton is still two
objects; the eye counts them rather than reading one thing moving.

### Round 5 — whoosh

First attempt used round-capped strokes. **Verdict: "they look like stunted batons"** — correct,
and the reason is that a capsule is the baton's own vocabulary at a smaller size. Replacing them
with calligraphic strokes that taper at both ends fixed it.

Final four: `Dissipating`, `Slipstream`, `Drift`, `Wisp`. **`Wisp` chosen** — each stroke carries
an S-bend rather than a single arc, so the air curls instead of streaking.

### The bin

Drawn, rendered, rejected. Do not re-draw without a new reason.

| Direction                                           | Why it failed                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tapered comet baton                                 | Reads as a baseball bat                                             |
| Comet with a hot tip                                | Reads as a match or torch                                           |
| Heavily curved baton                                | Reads as a banana                                                   |
| Arrows (shaft + chevron)                            | Generic, and the chevron arms broke the 75 px margin                |
| Open ring catching the baton                        | The ring swallows the baton; reads as a horseshoe or magnet         |
| Crescent "hands" at each end                        | Reads as decoration, not as hands                                   |
| Spin ring around the tail                           | Reads as a keyring or lollipop                                      |
| Crossing batons                                     | Reads as scissors or a checkmark                                    |
| Baton plus a single dot                             | Reads as a rotated exclamation mark — which is a sibling app's mark |
| Speed lines fanned at mixed angles                  | Scattered; no read                                                  |
| Speed lines at a mid angle                          | Stack into clutter                                                  |
| Split-field tile (two blues, baton across the seam) | Bold, but says "crossing a boundary", not "pass"                    |
| Speed cuts across the baton                         | Reads as banding on a tube                                          |
| Three uniform speed lines                           | "Too uniform, too rigid, too static"                                |

### The gradient test

A real SVG `linearGradient` on the whooshes was drawn and rendered. At full size it works. At the
~20 px the admin navigation uses it turns to mud, and it pushes against Shopify's "bold colors and
simple patterns". The shipped mark fakes the fade with three solid tints instead, which drop away
cleanly at small size and leave the white stroke carrying the mark. **A fourth tint is how the
fade turns back into mud.**

Jet or rocket exhaust was raised and not pursued: a plume that reads as exhaust needs a nozzle to
emit from, and a nozzle is furniture bolted to the baton — round 3's failure, rebuilt.

---

## 6. Picking this back up

The look is not final. To resume:

1. Open the design canvas if it still exists — the review artifact carried each round's variants,
   a 16/20/32/48 px size test against `#FFFFFF` and `#F1F1F1`, and a compliance board. If it is
   gone, the size test is the thing worth rebuilding first; it settled more arguments than any
   full-size comparison did.
2. Read §5's rules and bin before drawing. The three rules in §1 are the ones that survived five
   rounds of review; the bin is 14 directions that did not.
3. Edit `VARIANTS` in `scripts/icon.ts`, run `pnpm icon`, and read the printed `fit:` line.
4. Render at small sizes and look, every time. Four separate errors in this work — the
   overlapping capsules, the lopsided rails, the claw-shaped whooshes, the blank-tile
   rasterisation — were invisible in the geometry and obvious in the render.

Open questions worth a decision next time:

- Does the mark need a wordmark lockup? The login page currently pairs mark and name by hand.
- Is the amber right? It has never been tested against alternatives on the cobalt ground; the
  colour rounds only ever compared _grounds_ (ink, cobalt, clay, plum, bone — cobalt chosen).
- Does the landing page's 56 px mark still work once there is real landing copy around it? It is
  the only placement that has never been reviewed against a finished page.
